data.name: Embers of Magic
data.detailed_description:
Embers of Magic is a short, adventure visual novel that tells the story of Liana the witch. She takes an airship down to the surface of the dangerous and corrupt earth beneath her flying city home.


It is set in the same world as Brilliant Shadows, but happens 300 years beforehand.


Writing by Christopher "Nyo" Michael Hall
Artist/Coding by Sita "Geckos" Duncan
Engine: Ren'Py
Composer: Caelem
Voices: Adoxographist, Alec Shea, Nyo, Brad Smith and many others...
Embers of Magic is a kinetic novel lasting around 30 minutes. All spoken lines are fully voiced. It is 6,262 words in length.

reviews.review:
Embers of Magic is a very short visual novel that caught my attention mostly because of its setting. I follow Liana, a witch who leaves her home in a flying city and takes an airship down to the dangerous world below. The idea of a civilisation living above a corrupted Earth is interesting, and I like the contrast between the strange magical world above and the much darker place Liana is travelling into. It is a simple setup, but it gives the story a nice sense of mystery from the beginning.

The biggest strength for me is the atmosphere. The game has its own fantasy setting and does a good job making the short story feel like it belongs to a much larger world. It is also connected to Brilliant Shadows, although this story takes place 300 years earlier, so there is some extra background for me to appreciate if I want to look further into the setting. I like when a short game gives me the feeling that there is more history behind what I am seeing instead of explaining absolutely everything straight away.

The voice acting is another strong point. Every spoken line is fully voiced, which makes a noticeable difference in something this short because I am spending most of my time following the characters and their conversations. The music also helps with the mood without becoming the main focus. The whole presentation feels more like a small animated story than a traditional game, and I think that suits the idea much better than trying to add unnecessary gameplay systems.

The main problem is the length. The entire story is only around 30 minutes and is described as a kinetic novel, so there is not really much interaction or choice involved. I can mostly sit back and follow the story rather than actively playing. That is not necessarily a bad thing, but it does mean I have to judge the game more like a short visual story than an adventure game. I would have liked more time with Liana and more opportunities to explore the world because the setting feels like it has potential that the short runtime never really gets to use.

I also think the story moves too quickly for some of its ideas to have as much impact as they could. The concept of the flying city, the dangerous Earth below and Liana's journey are all interesting, but I never get a huge amount of time to properly understand the world or the characters. The writing has to introduce the setting, establish the situation and reach its ending in a very small amount of time. Because of that, some parts feel more like an introduction to a larger story than a complete adventure by themselves.

Still, I have to give Embers of Magic credit for being completely free and for knowing exactly what it wants to be. It is not pretending to be a huge RPG or an interactive adventure with dozens of hours of content. It is a short, fully voiced visual story with its own fantasy setting, artwork and music. If I approach it expecting a full game, the lack of interaction and very short length are obvious problems. If I approach it as a quick piece of world building and storytelling, I can appreciate it much more.

Overall, Embers of Magic is a decent little visual novel that has a much more interesting setting than its short runtime gives it room to explore. I like Liana's journey, the flying city concept, the darker world below and the fully voiced presentation. The biggest issue is simply that there is not enough here. I finish it just as the world starts becoming interesting, and I would have preferred a longer story with more character development and exploration. Even so, it is free, easy to get through and has enough atmosphere to make the short experience worthwhile.

Rating: 6.8/10
